authorization.verbatim: 你来主导完成阶段二，我看结果
authorization.scope: Autonomously complete S014 phase two; no phase-three strategy/account construction

data.access: Pinned native S014 DFLS assets and published EX004 EvidenceRefs only

selection_history: Designed after EX004 findings and the observed 2026 coverage problem; all periods remain seen development data.
questions: Do score and feature distribution shifts, fixed annual thresholds and one-event dependence explain the old reversal/risk clues?
Does causal recalibration rescue incremental information, or only increase coverage without better ranking?
Do fixed pullback-turn, breakout-volume or shock-close mechanisms provide usable information beyond their simpler parent condition?
Does persistent volatility offer a risk-scale role beyond same-day range, independent of avoiding fills?

chronology.training: Expanding 2020 history; only labels with actual maturity strictly before test-year first signal
chronology.new_rule_warmup: 60 sessions inside the window; no external prehistory
chronology.features: Completed T only; execute on T+1
chronology.states: ret20 >= 0 vs < 0, crossed with std20 above vs below training-year median
chronology.limitations: Not historical publication/revision verification or independent holdout

old_model_audit.replication: Reproduce EX004 fixed fits and all saved test predictions before using scores
old_model_audit.causal_recalibration: Same annual fitted model; threshold from predictions on strictly preceding 63 sessions, 75th percentile for returns and 25th for risk. No current or future score enters threshold.
diagnostics: paired-block uncertainty with recomputed selection denominators

pullback_turn.hypothesis: A completed up day after an uptrend pullback distinguishes stabilization from continued decline

breakout_volume.parent: Close > maximum High of preceding 20 sessions
breakout_volume.component: parent and Volume > mean Volume of preceding 20 sessions
breakout_volume.hypothesis: Volume confirmation distinguishes participation from a weak breakout

shock_close.parent: ret1 <= 10th percentile of mature training-sample ret1
shock_close.hypothesis: An upper-half close after a large down day distinguishes absorption from continued pressure

risk_scale.parent: range1 <= 25th percentile of strictly preceding 252 sessions
risk_scale.component: std20 <= 25th percentile of strictly preceding 252 sessions
risk_scale.hypothesis: Persistent realized volatility predicts next-holding-period adverse movement better than the current day's range
risk_scale.conditional_check: Within each of four training-defined range bins, measure std20/adverse Spearman association, counts and returns

fixed_mechanisms.interpretation: Mechanism rules are component event selections, not complete strategies. No parameters are searched or chosen from outcomes. Same-source conditional expressions do not create independent information.

comparisons.composition: 8 old-model pairs (2 horizons x 2 roles x fixed/recalibrated) + 9 event-confirmation pairs (3 mechanisms x 3 horizons) + 3 risk-scale pairs
comparisons.uncertainty: 5000 paired 20-session circular block resamples within each test year; recalculate selected means and counts in every draw. Empty selection draws remain missing and valid-draw fractions are reported. Report ordinary 95 percent and family-20 intervals alongside the previous 32 comparisons and adaptive history.
comparisons.pooling: Eligible-date-weighted mean of per-year selected-minus-control means; positive risk difference means less adverse movement
comparisons.robustness: Leave each year out; report top-positive-day removal and year/state sample counts; these are diagnostics, not new economic gates
comparisons.judgment: Researcher weighs incremental effects, counts, cross-state/year behavior, rank evidence and economic tradeoffs; no statistical or frequency acceptance threshold is invented

precheck: Public input identity; preserved prior EvidenceRefs; fixed-fit replication; serial/spawn equality; new-feature and rolling-threshold prefix causality; no network allowed
closure: Resolve the coverage/state question, classify supported, ineffective, redundant or insufficient components with necessary counterevidence; follow any material new clue within phase two before final judgment. Negative/empty panel is allowed. Publish successor COMPONENTS revision and copy its report exactly.
